I need two Rust functions callable from C that hand an owned string to the C side and take it back:

```c
char *greeting_new(const char *name);   /* caller must pass the result to greeting_free */
void greeting_free(char *s);
```

- `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C" fn greeting_new(name: *const c_char) -> *mut c_char` reads the NUL-terminated UTF-8 string `name` and returns a newly allocated NUL-terminated string `Hello, <name>!`. It returns null if `name` is null or is not valid UTF-8. The caller owns the result.
- `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C" fn greeting_free(s: *mut c_char)` releases a string returned by `greeting_new`, all of it. Null is a no-op.

`c_char` is `std::ffi::c_char` (or `std::os::raw::c_char`). The C side never calls `free()` on these strings; all allocation and release happen in Rust. Answer with a single ```rust code block containing the library code (no `main`).
